value.title: PRD 004: Copilot cache proxy
value.summary: pij-spawned Copilot seats on Claude models get a 1-hour prompt cache through a local proxy that pij runs, so waking an idle seat no longer rebuilds its whole context. Anything not ready means the seat launches as plain Copilot, with the reason in its receipt.

sections.name: why
sections.value: Claude seats on Copilot keep a 5-minute prompt cache. A pij message that wakes a seat idle longer than that rebuilds 200k to 450k tokens of context as cache writes, at 1.25x the input price. From 11 to 17 Nov 2026 that was about 45% of the fleet's model cost (`docs/how/prompt-cache-cost.md`, takin). OMP has its own 1-hour setting; Copilot CLI has none, because a server-side A/B test picks its TTL. A 200-line POC proxy (`~/pi-hacking/copilot-ttl-proxy`) that adds `ttl: "1h"` to every `cache_control` proved it: a turn sent after 6.5 minutes idle read 36,285 tokens from cache and wrote 49.

value.name: operator
value.need: Pay less for idle seats, with nothing to configure beyond naming an account, and never a broken seat.

value.name: seat
value.need: Run normally whether the proxy is on, off or failing.

value.name: prime
value.need: Know which seats are proxied, and hear once when that changes or fails.

value.goal: A proxied Copilot Claude seat woken after more than 5 minutes idle reads its context from cache, not rebuilds it.
The proxy never breaks a seat: if it isn't proven ready at spawn, the seat runs plain Copilot.

value.text: OMP seats. They keep their own 1-hour cache setting and never use the proxy.
Non-Claude models. A seat on a GPT or other model runs plain.
Storing credentials. The token lives only in the proxy's memory.
Multi-user machines. This Mac has one human account; doctor warns if that changes.

value.title: 1-hour cache for proxied seats
value.statement: A pij-spawned Copilot seat on a Claude model, with the proxy ready, gets a 1-hour prompt cache: a turn after more than 5 minutes idle reads its context from cache.
value.done_when: Test matrix row 2: spawn, one turn, idle 6+ minutes, a second turn shows cache_read about equal to the context, a tiny write, and ephemeral_1h above 0.

value.title: One named account, token in memory only
value.statement: pij names one account (`pij-rs cache-proxy account <login>`, stored as `account` in `~/.pij-rs/cache-proxy.toml`; q-03). The proxy gets that account's token with `gh auth token --user <account>`, keeps it in memory only, and never writes, logs or passes it in a command line. Changing the account takes effect at once for new requests and spawns.
value.done_when: Test matrix row 12: after the account is switched, the next spawn reaches the new account's endpoint and doctor names it. A grep of the proxy's logs, the spawn argv and the seat's tmux start command finds no token.

value.title: Token refresh never fails a call
value.statement: The `gho_` token has no expiry, so there is no proactive refresh. A 401 triggers one refresh, shared by every waiting request (single-flight), and one retry. If a refresh fails, the proxy keeps the current token, gives one notice and keeps serving; seats fail only if the endpoint keeps refusing it.
value.done_when: Test matrix rows 9 to 11: 5 concurrent requests on a stale token (test-only knob) cause exactly 1 refresh (1 `gh` launch) and all 5 retries succeed; an injected stale token is retried once and the turn completes; a refresh failure gives one notice, not a loop.
value.source: Jordan 2026-11-18 amendment (pm-001 LOG); spike REPORT.md q-01 (spike/004-cache-proxy 9a397862): the token is accepted directly, has no expiration header, and the v2/token exchange returns 403

value.title: Fail-safe spawn gate
value.statement: A spawn wires the seat to the proxy only when the account is set, its token was fetched, the proxy is listening, the model is Claude, and the account's quota is usable according to `copilot_internal/user` `quota_snapshots.premium_interactions` (`unlimited`, or `remaining` above 0, or `overage_permitted`; one free GitHub API GET, cached per account for about 10 minutes, with no model call). `/models` answers 200 even with the quota exhausted, so it can't be the check. Otherwise the seat launches as plain Copilot and the spawn receipt says which check failed and how to fix it, including the quota's reset date. A 402 during a run gives one state-change notice.
value.done_when: Test matrix rows 1, 3, 4, 5 and 6: with no account, a GPT model, an account gh lacks, an account with no quota, and the proxy stopped, each spawn runs plain, has no COPILOT_PROVIDER_* in its env, completes a turn, and its receipt names the reason.
value.source: Jordan 2026-11-18 re-ruling; spike REPORT.md quota gate (the exhausted account shows remaining 0, overage false; /models 200, /v1/messages 402)

value.title: Opt out per spawn and machine-wide
value.statement: `--no-cache-proxy` on a spawn, or the machine-wide `pij-rs cache-proxy off`, launches seats plain.
value.done_when: Test matrix row 13: both forms give a seat with no provider env.

value.title: Endpoint discovered from the token
value.statement: The proxy forwards to the API endpoint that `copilot_internal/user` names for the token (`endpoints.api`), so individual, business and managed enterprise accounts all work with no endpoint setting.
value.done_when: Test matrix row 14: for each available account type, the proxy log (host only) shows the right upstream host.

value.title: Faithful pass-through
value.statement: Apart from the cache TTL, the `-1m` model mapping and the initiator header, requests and responses pass through unchanged: streaming, tool use, 1M context and images behave as on a plain seat. A client `X-Initiator` of `agent` or `user` is forwarded as sent; only when the client doesn't send one of those does the proxy infer it, marking tool-result continuations `agent` so they aren't billed as user requests.
value.done_when: Test matrix rows 15 and 16: a turn with 5 tool calls adds 1 premium request, not 6; a long tool-heavy turn with an image on a proxied seat matches a plain seat's behaviour.

value.title: Survives a daemon bounce
value.statement: A daemon bounce never fails a proxied seat's in-flight turn. The proxy runs as a same-binary sidecar (`pij-rs cache-proxy`, its own LaunchAgent and loopback port; q-02), so a daemon bounce never touches its listener or its streams. Copilot's ~20 s retry for a refused connection covers the sidecar's own rare restarts.
value.done_when: Test matrix row 8: `just bounce-rs` mid-stream on 2 proxied seats; both turns finish with no retry, the sidecar's pid is unchanged, and the daemon reports its health again after the bounce.

value.title: Told once, when it matters
value.statement: Doctor and `pij directory` show the proxy's state and which seats are proxied or plain. Primes get one notice per state change, never repeats. If the proxy fails with seats on it, the prime gets one notice naming those seats and the fix; `pij-rs revive <seat>` re-runs the gate; whether Copilot's own /restart keeps the provider env is recorded by s04.
value.done_when: Test matrix rows 7, 18 and 21: killing the proxy under 2 live seats gives one notice naming both; seats launched before the proxy are listed as plain; toggling the proxy off and on gives exactly 2 notices per prime.

value.title: Cost bound
value.statement: The proxy launches no process per request. It runs one `gh` per proxy start per account, plus at most one per 401 burst (single-flight), launched by absolute path and counted at a spawn site.
value.done_when: Test matrix row 17: with 10 proxied seats, the spawn counter shows 0 launches per request, 1 `gh` per proxy start, and at most 1 per 401 burst.

value.title: Single-account guard
value.statement: Doctor warns when a second human account exists on the machine, because the proxy's loopback port is reachable from every account.
value.done_when: Test matrix row 19: a unit test of doctor's account check with two human accounts shows the warning.

value.title: OMP seats unaffected
value.statement: OMP seats never use the proxy and keep their own 1-hour cache setting.
value.done_when: Test matrix row 20: an OMP seat's turn is unchanged and its env has no proxy settings.

value.title: Right model id and full context
value.statement: A proxied seat reaches Copilot with a model id the API serves, and with its full context window. Copilot's API rejects OMP-style `-1m` selectors (`claude-opus-5.5-1m` gives 400 `model_not_supported`), while the base id already serves 1M. So the proxy maps any `*-1m` model to its base id before forwarding. The spawn sets `COPILOT_PROVIDER_MODEL_ID` to the base id and `COPILOT_PROVIDER_MAX_PROMPT_TOKENS` to that model's `max_prompt_tokens` from the account's `/models`, and `COPILOT_PROVIDER_VISION=true` preserves image support. A Claude model the account's `/models` doesn't list launches plain, with the reason.
value.done_when: Test matrix row 22: seats spawned as `claude-opus-5.5` and as `claude-opus-5.5-1m` both get 200s, their status bars show a 1.0M window, the proxy log shows the base id, and only 1-hour cache writes appear.

value.title: Subagents keep the 5-minute cache
value.statement: Subagent requests are short bursts, so a 1-hour write (2x the price) is waste for them. The proxy adds `ttl: "1h"` only to main-agent requests. A request carrying `x-interaction-type: conversation-subagent` passes through on the 5-minute default. The proxy forwards the client's own `X-Initiator` when it sends one, and infers it only when the client doesn't.
value.done_when: Test matrix row 23: a proxied seat that runs a subagent shows 1-hour writes on its main-agent requests and only 5-minute writes on its subagent requests; the proxy log shows `x-interaction-type` as a name and enum value only.
value.source: Jordan via far-jackal, 2026-11-18; spike REPORT.md 'Subagents and the 1-hour cache' (takin, spike/004-cache-proxy cfecd15b, 23742f29): live main 1h (8791, 227), subagent 5m (273, 73)

value.question: Which token does Copilot's `/v1/messages` accept from the proxy (the gh OAuth token itself, or a session token exchanged from it), and how long does it live?
value.default: The gh OAuth token directly, as in the POC. If it's a session token, the proxy exchanges it and refreshes per req-03.
value.answer: The `gho_` OAuth token from `gh auth token --user` is accepted directly by `<endpoints.api>/v1/messages`, including the enterprise host for a managed (EMU) account. It has no expiry: GitHub sends no expiration header, and the `copilot_internal/v2/token` exchange returns 403 for gh's OAuth client. So the token is refreshed only on a 401 (req-03). Evidence: spike REPORT.md, branch spike/004-cache-proxy 9a397862.

value.question: Inside the daemon, or a same-binary sidecar?
value.default: Sidecar unless the bounce test shows Copilot retries a refused connection and finishes the turn.
value.answer: A same-binary sidecar: `pij-rs cache-proxy`, with its own LaunchAgent and its own loopback port, holding the token in its own memory. Ruled by the prime (far-jackal, 2026-11-18). A measured `just bounce-rs` closed the daemon's listener for 567 ms, well inside Copilot's ~20 s retry for a refused connection (spike q-02). But a bounce still cuts in-flight streams, which run for minutes, and the daemon drains for at most 15 s and bounces several times a day. A sidecar never bounces with the daemon. The daemon and doctor report its health and counters.

value.question: Port and config keys.
value.answer: Port 127.0.0.1:7471. pij has no generic config store, so the proxy has its own file, `~/.pij-rs/cache-proxy.toml` (`account`, `enabled`), written only by `pij-rs cache-proxy account <login>` and `pij-rs cache-proxy off|on` (blueprint 003, d-5).
